claims.text: Increasing the number of rare-earth elements mixed at the RE site from one to five progressively increases configurational entropy.
Mixing multiple rare-earth elements creates local chemical disorder at the RE site.
Rare-earth-site chemical disorder induces local lattice strain.
Rare-earth-site disorder alters the local electronic environment.
Entropy-induced strain fields enhance electron–phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron–phonon coupling increases superconducting pairing efficiency in REBa2Cu3O7-δ.
Intermediate-to-high RE-site configurational entropy increases critical current density relative to a single-RE baseline.
Four- and five-RE samples can have higher local critical current density than zero- or low-entropy samples at 2.0–4.2 K.
Increasing RE-site configurational entropy may modestly enhance or optimize Tc.
Superconducting performance should vary non-monotonically with disorder, improving to an optimum and then degrading.
Excessive RE-site disorder creates scattering centers.
Disorder-induced scattering centers suppress superconductivity beyond an optimal entropy level.
The beneficial effect of configurational entropy requires maintained oxygen stoichiometry.
A single-RE REBa2Cu3O7-δ sample has minimal configurational entropy at the RE site.
Polycrystalline REBa2Cu3O7-δ samples with different RE-site mixing entropies can be synthesized by solid-state reaction.
Oxygen-content variation can affect the measured superconducting properties and confound the entropy comparison.
The identity of the constituent rare-earth elements may affect reproducibility independently of configurational entropy.
The experiment will compare one- through five-RE samples under nominally identical synthesis and oxygen-control conditions.
Failure to observe an initial Jc and/or Tc enhancement followed by degradation across the tested series would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The optimal entropy level is explicitly stated to be unknown, yet the experiment only tests one through five RE elements and treats absence of a non-monotonic optimum within that finite range as falsification. If the optimum lies beyond the tested range, a monotonic trend would not logically falsify the hypothesis.
